guarantees.claim: hw2reg.err_code.d is assigned the concatenation {code, info} of the highest priority error source with valid=1; if no source valid, assigned 0.
guarantees.cond: priority order: app_err > errchecker_err > sha3_err > entropy_err > msgfifo_err

assumptions.claim: When any x_err.valid is asserted, the corresponding x_err.code and x_err.info must be stable and valid; glitches or transitions while valid is high may produce transient erroneous error codes.
assumptions.cond: any clock cycle where an error source valid is high
assumptions.risk: The subsequent register (hw2reg.err_code) may capture an incorrect error code, causing false error responses or masking real errors.

uncertain_points.claim: The priority case discards lower priority error sources when multiple valid signals are asserted simultaneously. It is unclear if this loss is intentional or if a separate mechanism should capture all concurrent errors.
uncertain_points.cond: Multiple error valid signals high at the same time
uncertain_points.risk: Critical lower priority errors could go unlogged or unhandled, potentially hiding security or functional faults.

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational assignment of hw2reg.err_code.d may be sensitive to glitches on any error valid, code, or info signal if they are not synchronous and stable; this could cause a false error code to be latched.
uncertain_points.cond: Asynchronous or glitchy transitions on error source signals
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious error code capture leading to false alarms or masked real errors.
